summary: Reproduced the dLLM volatile-block ownership defect in the checked-out classic RadixCache with real paged pools: two denoise keys made 128 tokens of tree accounting refer to only 96 tokens of distinct physical pages. The correction excludes dllm_incomplete_ids from unfinished-request radix insertion until the block resolves, and applies this to both classic RadixCache and the current UnifiedRadixCache path. Related upstream PRs #35470 and #35781 were inspected before implementation.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before ownership/accounting regression. Classic RadixCache reported 128 accounted tokens for 96 tokens of distinct owned physical pages; the unified fixture also exposed missing fix/API state before source changes. Raw output: reports/j-d58e7286dc7e/raw/failing-before.log

54 tests and 61 subtests passed, including classic and unified physical-page ownership regressions, resolved-block behavior, a short non-dLLM boundary, and existing radix lock/free contracts. Raw output: reports/j-d58e7286dc7e/raw/focused-tests.log

tests.command: rocminfo; Python torch CPU/GPU float32 reduction comparison
tests.what_was_measured: The assigned accelerator reports gfx950 / AMD Instinct MI350X. A 4096-element float32 squared-sum matched the independent CPU Torch result exactly (22898102272.0). This validates GPU availability only, not the unavailable LLaDA serving reproduction. Raw output: reports/j-d58e7286dc7e/raw/gfx950-evidence.log

gpu_execution.evidence: A numerical Torch operation executed on the assigned gfx950 and matched the CPU reference exactly; the issue-specific regression itself is allocator/tree logic and ran deterministically on CPU paged pools.

remaining_limitations: LLaDA2.1 model weights and an Ascend NPU were not available, so the original 256-request HTTP serving workload was not rerun.
The GPU check is only a device/numerical smoke and is not claimed as a full-model reproduction.

The correction covers classic RadixCache and UnifiedRadixCache, the directly reproduced and current default paths. SWA, Mamba, and experimental C++ radix caches were not exercised with dLLM and remain outside this narrow change.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
